newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo keeps right to act against foreign brokers.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo keeps right to act against foreign brokers.

text.p: A Sumitomo Corp spokesman said on Thursday the company retains the right to file legal complaints against foreign metal brokers that dealt with its former copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
On Tuesday, Sumitomo managing director Naoki Kuroda told reporters the company had found no evidence that would lead it to file such complaints.
"What he wanted to say was that we had not found any evidence at this stage of an internal investigation. But we still hold the right to file legal complaints if necessary," Sumitomo spokesman said.
"Everything depends on our internal investigation," the spokesman said. He declined to elaborate.
Tokyo prosecutors on Tuesday arrested Hamanaka for forgery and raided his home in a Tokyo suburb.
Hamanaka was fired in mid-June when Sumitomo announced massive losses from alleged unauthorised copper trades. The losses are now estimated at $2.6 billion.
